title: Emergency throughput regression: token/sec drop across medium models after scheduler rollout
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Multiple production customers reported a sudden degradation in tokens/sec (up to 60% drop) and increased TTFT for medium-sized conversational workloads (seq_len 512-2048) after the runtime-1.19 scheduler/kernel-selection rollout on 2026-03-09. Affected deployments span Hosted API, two Dedicated pools, and one Private customer (VPC).

Observed behavior:
- Token/sec dropped from ~950 tok/s -> ~380 tok/s on NVLink A100 nodes for the mid-range models (redwood/open-mid-*-13B variants).
- TTFT for single-turn responses increased from median 140ms -> 320ms for many requests.
- Tail latency (p99) spiked by 3x in the Hosted cluster serving mixed-short/long tails.
- Degradation surfaced after enabling the new "adaptive-schedule-v2" kernel selector and the dynamic batching heuristics intended to reduce GPU fragmentation.

Hypothesis so far:
- The new scheduler is aggressively coalescing small requests with large sequences, causing long token-generation strides to hold CUDA streams and KV cache lanes, starving other small requests (head-of-line blocking).
- On Dedicated and Private nodes there is an interaction between the kernel choice (fast-but-large-kernel) and our continuous-batching codepath that increases per-token cost when sequence length variance is high.

Why this is urgent:
- Three strategic customers reported SLA violations and opened escalations. One customer temporarily disabled production traffic to avoid customer-facing errors. This is causing revenue and trust risk.

Desired outcome:
- Restore previous tokens/sec/TTFT for affected models within the next 48 hours, minimize customer impact, and ship a root-cause fix and regression tests before releasing adaptive-schedule-v2 broadly.
steps_taken: 2026-03-09 04:10 UTC: Pager alert - Hosted model cluster p99 latency breach. Notified SRE and runtime on-call.
2026-03-09 04:25 UTC: Rolled back adaptive-schedule-v2 flag in Hosted Canary (20% traffic) — initial improvement seen but not complete.
2026-03-09 05:00 UTC: Applied temporary routing rule to divert affected customer traffic to runtime-1.18 model variants and disabled dynamic batching on Dedicated pool DED-3.
2026-03-09 07:10 UTC: Private customer's ops team rolled back the runtime flag at their side after coordination; they report restoration of throughput.

2026-03-10 10:30 UTC: Reproduced locally with loadgen: when mixing short (16 token prompts) and long (2k token prompts) sequences, scheduler places large sequence requests first leading to lower aggregate tok/s.
2026-03-11 13:20 UTC: Implemented a short-term hotfix (PR #8421) that adds sequence-length-aware queue prioritization; landed behind a feature flag.
2026-03-12 02:05 UTC: Canary deploy of hotfix to Hosted Canary cluster; metrics show tokens/sec recovered to ~90% of baseline for mixed workloads.
2026-03-12 14:00 UTC: Hotfix promoted to Dedicated pool DED-3; Private customer scheduled for 2026-03-13 maintenance window.
2026-03-13 09:30 UTC: Monitoring shows improvement but p99 still ~1.6x baseline for a narrow tail; added follow-up to fully address kernel-choice regression.
impact: High. Affected: 3 customers with production traffic + a broad set of Hosted tenants on mixed-traffic clusters. Estimated revenue-at-risk during incident: medium-high. Operational: increased on-call time, customer success escalations.
metrics_snapshot: Baseline tokens/sec (mid models): 900-1000 tok/s; during regression: 320-420 tok/s; post-hotfix: 820-920 tok/s. TTFT median baseline: 120-160ms -> regression: 280-360ms -> post-hotfix: 140-200ms.
comments: 2026-03-10 11:02 - Alejandro Ruiz: Added prioritization hotfix behind flag. Tests show reduced head-of-line blocking in synthetic mixed-load scenarios. Preparing PR.
2026-03-10 18:47 - Maya Chen (PM): Coordinated communications with CS for impacted customers. Drafted status update and recommended temporary credit for SLA miss.
2026-03-11 09:15 - Priya Nair (SRE): Canary metrics look promising but noticed p99 still elevated when background KV cache eviction occurs. Added observability spike.
2026-03-12 15:40 - Tomas Becker (infra): Observed that kernel selection favors 'large-block-optimized' on A100 when seq_len>1024; need a conservative kernel policy for mixed workloads.
2026-03-13 08:05 - Alejandro Ruiz: Hotfix promoted to Dedicated; scheduling full rollout contingent on additional regression tests listed below.
postmortem_next_steps: Complete root-cause analysis: interact with kernel-selection matrix and continuous-batching codepath (owner: Alejandro)
Add regression tests in CI that simulate mixed short/long sequences and assert tokens/sec baseline for target models (owner: QA)
Introduce conservative kernel policy toggle per pool that can prefer 'low-latency' kernels for mixed workloads (owner: Runtime-Kernels)
Update rollout playbook to include automatic traffic diversion and observable checks for tokens/sec when enabling scheduling flags (owner: SRE)
Customer follow-up: Post-incident report + proposed mitigations and SLA remediation (owner: Maya)
Schedule a purple-team session to rehearse similar scheduling changes in staging with production-like traffic mix (owner: Eng Ops)
blocked_reason: Awaiting final kernel policy decision from Runtime-Kernels team to complete full rollout of adaptive-schedule-v2 replacement.
notes: Hotfix (PR #8421) reverts aggressive coalescing behavior and adds sequence-length-aware queueing. Longer-term fix requires kernel-selection heuristics. Keep customers informed per CS playbook.
